question: Which filesystem access boundary should OpenClaw support for host-mode agents: full allow/deny rules, roots with access modes, file-tools-only policy plus a separate exec policy, or no granular host policy beyond `workspaceOnly`?
rationale: This cannot be safely resolved by automation because it adds a new config surface and security boundary, and the open candidate PRs propose different shapes while leaving different gaps.

options.title: Approve a unified policy design
options.body: Define the canonical config shape and required coverage across file tools, media, apply_patch, subagents, and exec before landing implementation.

options.title: Split file tools and exec
options.body: Allow a file-tool policy to land only if docs and follow-up tracking make shell-mediated access explicitly out of scope.

options.title: Keep workspaceOnly only
options.body: Decline granular host path rules and steer users to Docker, OS isolation, and existing tool deny profiles.

recommendation.title: Approve a unified policy design
recommendation.body: Define the canonical config shape and required coverage across file tools, media, apply_patch, subagents, and exec before landing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the maintainer-side review framing for this issue and is the strongest current routing signal for the config/security boundary decision.
